The Hazelwood PS 4 6 bus tie 220kV notice gives 2026-08-20 11:00 AEST (2026-08-20T01:00:00Z), after the price extreme: interval ending 2026-08-19T23:10:00Z = 2026-08-20 09:10 AEST (UTC+1000).

possible_explanations.statement: Local tightening of supply (higher dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the 5-minute peak [ev0437] and high operational demand in the half‑hour [ev0912]) may have contributed to the high RRP.

possible_explanations.statement: A binding network constraint or transfer limit change (the Hazelwood PS 4 6 bus tie 220kV outage notice exists [c1]) might have limited local transfer capability and so could have influenced prices; however the retrieved notice records the outage at 2026-08-20 11:00 AEST (2026-08-20T01:00:00Z) which is after the 2026-08-19T23:10:00Z price extreme [c1].
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain AEMO constraint binding logs and the precise Network Outage Scheduler start/end timestamps for the Hazelwood PS 4–6 bus tie to see if any Hazelwood‑related constraint or transfer limit was active during 2026-08-19T23:00:00Z–2026-08-19T23:15:00Z.

possible_explanations.statement: A generator trip or reductions in local generation (unit changes shown in SCADA summaries such as MURRAY +517.7 MW change in the 17:30–23:30Z window [ev0949]) could be consistent with an availability change that might affect price.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Check unit‑level SCADA/availability and outage logs and generator offer/bid changes for the interval around 2026-08-19T23:10:00Z to identify any sudden outages or large output changes coincident with the price spike.
